# Dialog

A window over the page that takes attention until people finish or close it.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-dialog--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:light" title="Dialog examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-dialog--docs">Open Dialog in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-dialog--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Edit one record without leaving the table.

- **Use it when:** People must decide or finish something before going back: a short form, an important choice.
- **Not when:** A short status (toast), extra detail on the page (accordion), or a side panel that should not block the page (sheet).

Instead:

- [Sheet](./sheet.md): A side panel; the page stays in view.
- [Toast](./toast.md): Does not interrupt.
- [Alert dialog](./alert-dialog.md): Confirms something that cannot be undone.

## How Dense data uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A menu or dialog</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> elevation.overlay and a dimmed page for dialogs</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A border only</div></div><div class="cap">Floating things need a shadow so they read as on top.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Delete or remove</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button secondary, then confirm in a dialog with Button danger</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Button primary as the first step</div></div><div class="cap">Deleting is rare and costly; a confirm step catches mistakes.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Escape closes it. | undefined |
| undefined | Tab stays inside while it is open. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is a dialog with a title; the page behind is hidden from screen readers. undefined
- [ ] Focus moves in when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add dialog
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
